hints.content:
The key understanding here is that there isn't a single way to define "athletic achievement." Number of sports medals won can be a good measure of that. Percentage of students in sports club is also a good measure.

Now let's go over the options and see which of them might be used to describe "athletic achievements relative to the budget per student."

Definition | Analysis | Appropriate?
:- | :- | :-:
Number of sports medals won divided by budget per student | "Number of sports medals won" is a measure of athletic achievement. Dividing this by the budget per student gives us a good definition. | $\greenD{\text{Yes}}$
Number of sports medals won divided by teachers per student | "Number of sports medals won" is a measure of athletic achievement, but it's divided by the rate of teachers per student, and not by the budget per student. | $\redD{\text{No}}$
% of students in sports club divided by budget per student |  "% of students in sports club" is a measure of athletic achievement. Dividing this by the budget per student gives us a good definition. | $\greenD{\text{Yes}}$
% of students in sports club divided by graduation rate | "% of students in sports club" is a measure of athletic achievement, but it's divided by the graduation rate, and not by the budget per student. | $\redD{\text{No}}$

We are left with two definitions for athletic achievements relative to the budget per student:

1. Number of sports medals won divided by budget per student
2. % of students in sports club divided by budget per student

Let's calculate the athletic achievements relative to the budget per student for each school according to each definition:

School | Definition #1 | Definition #2
:-: | :-: | :-:
A | $\approx 0.00086\,\dfrac{\text{student medals}}{\text{dollar}}$ | $\approx 0.0059\,\dfrac{\text{student percents}}{\text{dollar}}$
B | $0.0007\,\dfrac{\text{student medals}}{\text{dollar}}$ | $0.0068\,\dfrac{\text{student percents}}{\text{dollar}}$
Which school has higher athletic achievements relative to the budget per student? | School A | School B

question.content:
Analia is a school district manager. Here are some details about two schools in her district for the last school year:

 | School A | School B
:- | :-: | :-:
Number of students | $3000$ | $4000$
Number of teachers | $190$ | $380$
Graduation rate | $86\%$ | $90\%$
Budget per student | $\$10{,}500$ | $\$10{,}000$
% of students in sports club | $62\%$ | $68\%$
Number of sports medals won | $9$ | $7$
SAT average | $1200$ | $1050$
SAT range (max-min) | $900$ | $700$

Analia wants to know which school has higher athletic achievements relative to the budget per student.

**1) Analia thought of two different ways to define this quantity. Identify these two definitions among the following options.**

[[☃ radio 1]]

**2) Determine which school has higher athletic achievements relative to the budget per student, according to the two definitions. Did you get the same result for both definitions? **

[[☃ radio 3]]

choices.content: Number of sports medals won divided by budget per student
Number of sports medals won divided by teachers per student
% of students in sports club divided by budget per student
% of students in sports club divided by graduation rate
Yes. According to both definitions, School A has higher athletic achievements relative to the budget per student.
Yes. According to both definitions, School B has higher athletic achievements relative to the budget per student.
